title: Dynamic Treewidth
authors: Tuukka Korhonen (University of Bergen, Norway), Konrad Majewski (University of Warsaw, Norway), Wojciech Nadara (University of Warsaw, Norway), Michał Pilipczuk (University of Warsaw, Norway), Marek Sokołowski (University of Warsaw, Norway)
abstract: We present a data structure that for a dynamic graph $G$ that is updated by edge insertions and deletions, maintains a tree decomposition of $G$ of width at most $6k+5$ under the promise that the treewidth of $G$ never grows above $k$. The amortized update time is $O_k{2^{\sqrt{\log n}\log\log n}}$, where $n$ is the vertex count of $G$ and the $O_k{\cdot}$ notation hides factors depending on $k$. In addition, we also obtain the dynamic variant of Courcelle's Theorem: for any fixed property $\varphi$ expressible in the $CMSO_2$ logic, the data structure can maintain whether $G$ satisfies $\varphi$ within the same time complexity bounds. To a large extent, this answers a question posed by Bodlaender [WG 1993].
